title: runbook-linter-and-sidecar-sanity-prober
author: Priya Patel
description:
Adds a pre-merge runbook linter and a non-destructive sidecar sanity prober to reduce on-call friction and prevent dangerous runbook edits. Motivation: multiple post-incident rollbacks were traced to malformed or incomplete runbook steps (missing timeouts, missing rollbacks, plaintext secrets in examples). The linter enforces a small, opinionated policy surface (timeouts, required rollback step, redaction checks, approved command whitelist) and integrates as a fast GitHub Action. The sidecar prober runs as a staging-only job that exercises read-only telemetry queries and zero-impact verification of expected artifacts referenced by the runbook (config maps, dashboards, alert selectors) so we catch mismatches before a runbook is merged.

What changed (summary):
- New CLI tool `rb-lint` (Go) with rules: RULE_TIMEOUT_PRESENT, RULE_ROLLBACK_PRESENT, RULE_REDACT_EXAMPLES, RULE_WHITELISTED_CMDS. CLI returns machine-readable JSON and human-friendly summary.
- GitHub Action `runbook-lint.yml` that runs `rb-lint` on PRs touching `/runbooks/**` and fails the check on policy violations. Action is cached and horizontally parallel for large diffs.
- Sidecar prober service (lightweight Python worker) and Kubernetes Job manifest `runbook-prober-job.yaml` for staging. Prober performs read-only checks: validates referenced resource paths, queries Prometheus metrics to assert metric selectors exist, and validates that dashboard panels referenced by the runbook are resolvable. Prober intentionally does not execute any commands listed in runbooks.
- Unit tests for lint rules and an integration test that spins up a fake Prometheus and mock K8s API server to validate the prober's behavior.
- Docs: CONTRIBUTING.md additions describing how to author runbooks to satisfy lint rules and a new `docs/runbook-lint.md` with examples and remediation guidance.

Why this is safe: the linter is non-destructive; the prober uses read-only creds in staging only and is gated by an opt-in label `prober/staging-ok`. The GitHub Action gate prevents merging runbooks that fail policy checks unless an explicit `bypass/runbook-lint` label is present (requires two approvers).

Rollout plan: enable lint on all PRs in `incident-bot` repo first; enable the prober as an optional staged job for teams that opt-in for two weeks, then enable by default for staging deployments. We will monitor false positives and tighten rules over time.

Related work: ENG-1942 runbook hardening spike, ENG-1987 staging telemetry validation.

Notes on implementation trade-offs: the linter uses an allowlist-first approach for commands to keep the policy small; we purposely delayed adding a full DSL for runbook assertions to iterate on rules. The prober is intentionally conservative (read-only) to minimize blast radius.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement rb-lint rules and CLI
- [x] Add GitHub Action pipeline
- [x] Implement sidecar prober + k8s job manifest
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Docs and contributor guidance

Additional context for reviewers: pay attention to the redaction heuristics (heuristic-based regex) and give feedback if you see false positives for common multi-line examples. The `rb-lint` output includes file:line markers to make remediation quick.

notes: This PR reduces the frequency of rollout-causing runbook errors by catching structural problems early. Teams should follow docs/runbook-lint.md to update existing runbooks.
